intelligence.human_view: He named the feeling, not the fix: the name box is "just not impressive," and it should feel like something special — because that is where they enter the name of their land, their domain, their real estate. The treatment follows the feeling. The box becomes the deed itself: an elevated obsidian plaque with purple underglow, the typed name as the signature on the deed, the seal stamping on entry. One treatment in all three places — front page, identity page, agreement end — so the signing feels the same wherever they sign it. Everything is harvested, nothing invented: the identity seal-stamp, the Vault Dial v2 inputs, the name-as-royal-object look (obsidian middle, purple glow edges, chrome-thin white/silver trim, clone trick; gold OUT on the name), and the official sentence that says what the act means — "By entering your name, you make it official — you are signing the Collective Agreement, and you get the deed to your own world: high-level digital real estate." The sequencing is law, not preference: it fires AFTER the agreement-entrance-welcome round lands whole, because it touches the same files (`/` + `identity.html`) and the clobber law + deploy lock forbid two rounds on the same files at once; the base is the landed build, never a moving target. And the bookkeeping is honest: the One List add was attempted four times and failed four times on the EPERM flake — it has NOT landed, and the retry waits for the flake to clear. The brief is safe on disk; the work is queued, not lost.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you get a treasure map — but instead of a boring blank line, you sign your name on a shiny black plaque with purple glowing edges, like signing the deed to your very own castle! Your name appears in gold, and — STAMP! — a seal presses down, and the land is YOURS! That's how special your name should feel!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — when you sign for your house, dear, you don't scribble on a scrap of paper! You sign a proper deed, love — a beautiful dark plaque with a purple glow, your name in gold like a signature, and the seal stamps down with a thump! That's YOUR land, dear, YOUR domain — and the moment you write your name, it's official!
